# CLAUDE.md — Power BI Custom Visual (`.pbiviz`) Repository Governance & Workflow

This repository holds **one reusable Power BI custom visual**, versioned and released independently of any report that consumes it. It is a TypeScript repo, not a `.pbip` repo: there is no semantic model, no TMDL, no PBIR JSON, and no `pbi connect`. The governance below replaces the report-project governance wholesale — do not apply TMDL/PBIR rules here, and do not apply these rules to a report repo.

## 1. Step Zero & Conversational Language Policy

### A. Step Zero Mandatory Workflow Trigger
Before any construction work in this repo — triggers such as *"new visual"*, *"add a formatting option"*, *"change how it renders"*, *"package it"*, *"import it into the report"*, a sketch, or a list of requirements — invoke the **power-bi-visual-dev** skill BEFORE `power-bi-custom-visuals` or any other skill.

It is **step zero**: it establishes the canonical 6-stage order (Scope/Contract ➔ Capabilities & Data Roles ➔ Rendering ➔ Formatting Pane ➔ Build/Review/Package ➔ Distribute & Import), the host-independence premise, the Visual Validation Gate that stands in for a report's Desktop refresh, and the Git/Changelog checkpoint at each stage.

### B. Prompt Language vs Project Artifact Language
1. **Conversation Response Language:** Always reply in the **same language used in the user's prompt**.
2. **Project Artifact Language Alignment (Code & Metadata):** At Stage 1, confirm or ask which language governs TS code comments (`//`, `/** */`), user-facing strings, `pbiviz.json` `displayName`/`description`, and every `displayName` in the formatting model and `capabilities.json`. Maintain it consistently thereafter, regardless of the conversation language.
3. **Identifiers are never translated.** `name` values in the formatting model and `capabilities.json`, data-role names, property names, and TS symbols stay **English camelCase** in every project. Only `displayName` follows the Project Artifact Language — see Hard Rule #5 for why renaming an identifier later is destructive.

---

## 2. Custom Visual Skills Map

Authoring is **direct file editing** of `src/`, `capabilities.json`, `pbiviz.json`, and `style/`. The `pbiviz` CLI builds and packages; it never authors. Importing the compiled binary into a report is done by the report author.

The skills below are optional Claude Code skills from the maintainer's local setup; they are not part of this repo, and the rules in this file stand on their own without them.

- **power-bi-visual-dev** — Step zero for this repo: policies, the 6 canonical stages, the Visual Validation Gate, extraction from a host report, git checkpoints
- **power-bi-custom-visuals** — Construction: `pbiviz` build loop, `capabilities.json`, the mandatory `CompositeCard`/`Group` formatting-settings shape, `/code-review` pass, import into a report
- **power-bi-release** — Release lifecycle, Semver, `CHANGELOG.md` version cutting, annotated git tags (`vX.Y.Z`)
- **power-bi-themes** — The consuming report's `visualStyles` entry for this visual's registered `visualType`, and the theme colors the visual must read rather than hardcode
- **dataviz** (built-in) — Chart-form heuristic, mark specs, and palette construction. A custom visual *is* a chart: load this before choosing the encoding, the default palette, or a KPI/tile composition, exactly as a report visual would
- **artifact-design** (built-in) — Optional consumer-facing usage doc (data roles, format options, screenshots) for the report authors who will import this visual

Report-project skills (semantic model, DAX, TMDL/PBIR report authoring) **do not apply here**. If a task seems to need one, it belongs in a consuming report, not in this repo.

---

## 3. Standard Repository Layout

```
pbiviz.json                  ← visual metadata: guid (permanent), version, displayName, apiVersion
capabilities.json            ← dataRoles, dataViewMappings, objects (one entry per formatting card)
package.json  tsconfig.json  ← Node/TS toolchain (tsconfig.typecheck.json checks all of src/)
src/visual.ts                ← IVisual implementation: constructor + update()
src/settings.ts              ← formatting model (CompositeCard ➔ Group ➔ slices)
src/model/                   ← pure functions, no DOM; unit tests in src/**/__tests__
style/visual.less            ← styles
stringResources/             ← <locale>/resources.resjson; en-US must match defaultStrings in src/render/strings.ts
assets/icon.png              ← 20x20 pane icon
harness/                     ← headless harness page, mock host and synthetic data
tools/                       ← run-harness.mjs (Puppeteer), check-capabilities.mjs, check-sample.mjs, sync-sample-visual.mjs, generate_sample_data.py
samples/                     ← data/epc_progress.csv (generated) and report/ (PBIP with the visual embedded)
.github/workflows/           ← ci.yml (push/PR), release.yml (v* tags)
dist/                        ← build output (gitignored — see Hard Rule #13)
docs/BUILD_LOG.md            ← per-session log of what the AI and the maintainer did
docs/tasks/                  ← task specifications for Claude Code (read before acting)
CLAUDE.md  RELEASING.md  CHANGELOG.md  LICENSE
.gitattributes               ← forces LF on every text file (see Hard Rule #14)
```

**`capabilities.json` + the formatting model are the contract.** Everything a report author can bind or configure is declared there; `src/` may only read what the contract declares.

---

## 4. Hard Rules

### Identity & Versioning
1. **Never change `visual.guid` in `pbiviz.json`.** Power BI binds an imported visual to a report **by GUID**. Change it and every report already using this visual shows a missing-visual placeholder; re-importing under the new GUID does **not** restore the field bindings — every well has to be re-bound by hand, on every page, in every report. The `displayName` can be renamed freely; the GUID is permanent from the first import onward.
2. **`visual.version` in `pbiviz.json`, the `CHANGELOG.md` heading, and the git tag are one number.** Bump all three together, and only upward — the Power BI org store refuses to replace an imported visual with a lower version, and a mismatch makes "which build is in that report?" unanswerable. Four segments (`X.Y.Z.W`) is what `pbiviz` expects; keep the fourth at `0` unless a build counter is genuinely in use.

### Formatting Pane
3. **Every formatting card is a `CompositeCard` split into named `Group`s** — never the flat `SimpleCard` the `pbiviz new` scaffold emits. Convert before adding the second slice; retrofitting means renaming properties, which trips Hard Rule #5. Canonical card ➔ group taxonomy and the exact TS shape to copy: `power-bi-custom-visuals`.
4. **Property names must be unique across the whole card, not per group.** The formatting service builds every descriptor with `objectName = card.name`, so `capabilities.json` gets **one `objects` entry per card** listing every property of every group in that card, flattened. Two groups each declaring `fontSize` silently collapse onto one stored property.
5. **Never rename or retype a released property, data role, or card `name`.** Stored settings and field bindings are keyed by those identifiers inside each consuming report's PBIR JSON. A rename does not error — it silently resets every report author's saved configuration back to the default and drops their bound fields. Add a new property and read the old one as a fallback instead.

### Data & Rendering
6. **`update()` must survive every degenerate `dataView`.** Null `categorical`/`table`, zero rows, a missing measure, one category where the code assumed many, more series than colors. A bad `update()` renders an **empty rectangle, not an error** — the absence of a visible error is not evidence the handler works. Guard explicitly, and render a deliberate empty state.
7. **Clean up between updates.** `update()` fires on every resize, filter, and format change. Re-bind or null D3 event handlers, honor `.exit().remove()`, and never append to a container you did not clear — leaked listeners accumulate per update and fire N times on one click.
8. **Never hardcode a color.** Read the consuming report's theme through `host.colorPalette` (`getColor()`, `isHighContrast`, and the high-contrast members when set). A hardcoded palette makes this visual the one element on the page that ignores the report theme, and it fails accessibility mode outright. Colors chosen as *defaults* still come from a validated palette — load the built-in `dataviz` skill for that.
9. **No host-model assumptions.** The entire point of this repo is reuse across reports: no hardcoded field or measure names, no assumed number of series or categories, no assumed date grain, no assumed locale. Format numbers through `valueFormatter` with the column's own format string from the `dataView` metadata — never `toFixed` or a hand-built decimal separator.
10. **Interactivity goes through the host services, not the DOM.** Cross-filtering via `ISelectionManager` + `ISelectionIdBuilder`, tooltips via `host.tooltipService`, context menus via `selectionManager.showContextMenu()`. A DOM-only tooltip ignores the report's tooltip settings, escapes the visual's bounds, and behaves differently in the Service than in Desktop.

### Toolchain & Repo
11. **Certificate installation and Developer Mode are user actions.** `pbiviz --install-cert` touches the OS trust store and enabling *Developer mode* is a Power BI Service tenant setting — prompt for both, never run or assume them silently.
12. **Never hand-edit generated or managed files:** `.api/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/`, `package-lock.json`. Never bump `apiVersion` in `pbiviz.json` without moving `powerbi-visuals-api` to match — a mismatch either fails at package time or, worse, only in the Service at runtime, where there is no console to read.
13. **`dist/` is a build artifact and is gitignored; the released `.pbiviz` belongs to its tag.** Attach it to the GitHub release for `vX.Y.Z`, or without a remote keep it at `releases/vX.Y.Z/<VisualName>.pbiviz`. Exactly one traceable binary per version — a committed `dist/` guarantees the binary and the source drift apart with nothing to say which is current.
14. **Line endings are forced to LF via `.gitattributes`** (`*.ts`, `*.json`, `*.less`, `*.md`, `*.js`). Windows editors and the `pbiviz` toolchain both resave with CRLF; without the attribute a touched file becomes a full-file diff with zero real content change. A mass of modified files with an empty `git diff` is a CRLF flip, not real edits — normalize the line endings and re-diff before committing.

### Workflow & Quality
15. **Visual Validation Gate — this repo's substitute for a report's Desktop refresh.** Before any commit that changes `src/`, `capabilities.json`, or the formatting model, run `pbiviz start`, load the dev visual in Desktop, and confirm all of: renders with real data · renders deliberately with **zero rows** · renders with a **null/missing measure** · survives resize both directions · the Format pane shows **grouped** cards with working defaults · colors follow the report theme when the theme is switched. A green `pbiviz package` proves the code compiles, nothing more.
    **When `pbiviz start` is unavailable** — tools 7.x generates the dev certificate via PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`), which is not present on every machine — a headless test harness is an acceptable substitute for the data-shape half of this list (real data, zero rows, null measure, resize) and is strictly better than it for regression, because its checks are assertions rather than a human look. It does **not** cover the theme switch, high-contrast mode, real cross-filtering, or the Format pane as a report author sees it: those stay a human package-import-verify step and must never be reported as passed because the harness was green. A behavioral change with no new harness assertion is incomplete work.
16. **Never invoke `/code-review` or `/simplify` bare.** Every invocation states an **explicit effort level** and a **narrow target** (`src/`, one file, or a branch diff — never the repo root, which drags `node_modules/`, `.api/`, and `dist/` into the pass), and runs in a **fresh session** (`/clear` first). With no level given, `/code-review` silently reuses whichever level was typed last — one earlier `max` then reruns as `max` and can exhaust a session's tokens mid-pass, leaving no findings at all. Never run both in one session. `src/` is ordinary TypeScript, so unlike TMDL/PBIR these passes work at full strength here: run `/code-review medium src/` before every `pbiviz package` (Hard Rule #15 catches rendering defects; this catches the logic ones that still render), and reserve `high`/`max` for a deliberate pre-publish audit of a visual going out to many report authors.
17. **Branch when a change can break existing reports:** a data-role or capabilities change, a formatting-property change, an `apiVersion` bump. Additive rendering work can go on `main`.

---

## 5. Commit, Changelog & Release Protocol

Before finalizing any commit:

1. **Changelog Check:** If the work is consumer-visible (rendering, data roles, formatting options, defaults), add a one-line entry under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` and include it in the commit.
2. **Release Execution:** Claude Code cuts release headings and bumps versions on request or at a milestone — bumping `pbiviz.json` `visual.version` in the **same commit** as the heading (Hard Rule #2), renaming `[Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`, opening a fresh `[Unreleased]` above it, then:
   ```bash
   git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "<summary of changes>"
   ```
3. **Detection of Untagged Headings:** If a version heading `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` exists without a matching `vX.Y.Z` tag, Claude Code creates the annotated tag.
4. **Consumer Notification:** A MAJOR bump means existing reports need attention (see §6). Record in the changelog entry exactly what a report author must re-do after upgrading.

---

## 6. Visual-Adapted Semantic Versioning

The consumer of this repo is a **report author who has already bound fields and saved formatting**. Severity is measured by what breaks in *their* report, not by how much code changed.

| Bump  | Criteria |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MAJOR | Anything that invalidates an existing report's bindings or saved settings: a removed/renamed data role or property, a changed `dataViewMappings` shape, a required `apiVersion` bump, or a rendering change that alters the meaning of what was already published |
| MINOR | New data role (optional), new formatting card/group/property, new rendering capability — existing bindings and settings keep working untouched |
| PATCH | Rendering fixes, default-value corrections, `displayName`/label fixes, performance work, dependency bumps with no contract change |

---

## 7. Out of Scope for Claude Code

- Publishing to AppSource, submitting for Microsoft certification, org-store administration, and tenant Developer Mode — human only.
- Installing the dev certificate (`pbiviz --install-cert`) — prompt the user; it is their trust store.
- Fabricating data to make a rendering path look finished: build the branch with an explicit empty state and say it is unverified against real data.
- Changing `visual.guid` to "fix" an import problem (Hard Rule #1) — diagnose the import instead.

## Project Facts

- **Visual:** Physical Progress S-Curve (`physicalProgressSCurve`), GUID `physicalProgressSCurve1B810340E9DD4AE2BAA9AA4BF0E2FB5C`. Greenfield, open source (MIT), intended for public GitHub.
- **Project Artifact Language:** English for code, comments, identifiers, UI strings, docs and commit messages. pt-BR only through `stringResources/pt-BR`.
- **Contract source:** `SPEC.md` (written in Phase 1). Everything after Phase 1 is built against it.
- **Clean room:** build only from SPEC.md, the public Power BI visuals SDK docs and samples, and public library docs (D3, Vitest, Puppeteer). Never read, search or copy from any other visual's source, nor from client or employer projects. No client or employer names, real project data, or company URLs/emails anywhere; synthetic data only.
- **Never push, create remotes or publish** without the maintainer's explicit approval; show the exact commands first.
- **Never invent numbers** (time spent, users, feedback): use `TODO(igor): …` placeholders.
- **Commits** use the repo-local identity (`git config --local`), never the global one.
- **Toolchain:** Node 24 (CI and local), `powerbi-visuals-tools` pinned as a devDependency, API 5.11.1. `pbiviz start` works locally (PowerShell 7 generates the dev certificate into the user's personal store; trusting it with `pbiviz --install-cert` is a maintainer action). The headless harness is the automated data-shape half of the Visual Validation Gate (Hard Rule #15); the Desktop checks stay manual. **Never run `pbiviz package` while `pbiviz start` is running:** the dev server rewrites `.tmp/precompile/visualPlugin.ts` with a `<guid>_DEBUG` plugin name and the package picks it up (the harness GUID check fails when this happens). On Windows, stopping `npx pbiviz start` can leave the `pbiviz.js` node process alive on port 8080; kill it explicitly.
- **After a mutation check, rebuild before using `dist/`:** `npm run test:harness` repackages from whatever is in `src/` at the time, so the package left behind by a mutation run contains the mutation. Rebuild from the restored source before copying `dist/` anywhere.
- **Pinned on purpose:** `powerbi-visuals-utils-formattingutils` stays at 6.1.2. Version 7.0.0 ships its locale table as an ES module, and the localization loader in `powerbi-visuals-tools` 7.2.1 `eval`s it as CommonJS, so packaging fails. Revisit when the tools are upgraded.
- **Tests:** `npm test` runs `lint` (ESLint + `tsc -p tsconfig.typecheck.json` over all of `src/`) → `check:capabilities` → `test:unit` (Vitest, `src/**/__tests__`) → `test:harness` (`pbiviz package --resources`, then Puppeteer drives `harness/index.html` against the packaged JS). Fix failing tests in the code, never by weakening a test.
- **Governance block:** the section between the `power-bi-visual-skills` markers was adapted and sanitized from the maintainer's personal starter kit. Do not overwrite it from the kit; reconcile by hand.
- **Strings:** a new user-facing string goes in `defaultStrings` (`src/render/strings.ts`) and in both `stringResources` files, with the key `Visual_<key>`; unit tests fail if they differ or if a string is unused. Slices use `displayNameKey: resourceKey("...")`. The formatting library doesn't translate dropdown items or placeholders, so those hold a string key in `settings.ts` until `applySettings` translates them.
- **Locale formats ship per folder:** the packager keeps number and date formats only for en-US and for locales with a `stringResources/<locale>` folder, so 20 locales have an empty `{}` resource file just for that (SPEC Decision 14). Don't delete them as unused.
- **Sample report:** `samples/report` embeds a copy of the packaged visual, because a report can't open without it; it's the one build output in git, and it only moves at releases or on purpose (`npm run sample:sync`, after a clean `npm test`). `npm run check:sample` fails if its version differs from `pbiviz.json`, or if the report and the CSV disagree. Close the report in Desktop before editing its files: Desktop overwrites them when it saves.
- **Build log:** append an entry to `docs/BUILD_LOG.md` at the end of every working session.
